Phenomenon: Formal description of cognitive and social information processes
Method: Classical and quantum mechanics on p-adic information spaces; p-adic probability
Setup and data: Mathematical development with qualitative examples (associations, hierarchical social systems); no data
Key result: No empirical results; provides a p-adic formalism for information dynamics
Limitation: Speculative; no link to measured behaviour; p-adic approach not taken up by later QP cognition models

Phenomenon: Logical structure of disjunction; concept combination
Method: Quantum-logic analysis of 'or' via EPR-like correlation states and potentiality
Setup and data: Theoretical analysis of physical and macroscopic examples; cognitive application sketched
Key result: Quantum disjunction shown non-equivalent to classical 'or' owing to EPR-like correlations
Limitation: No data; cognitive implications only outlined

Phenomenon: Choice and response-time dynamics in decision-making
Method: Quantum random walk (Schrödinger evolution of amplitudes) vs Markov random walk
Setup and data: Analytical derivation of choice probabilities and response-time distributions
Key result: Quantum dynamics produce interference effects not possible under Markov models; predictions contrasted
Limitation: Largely theoretical; no dedicated experiment in this paper

Phenomenon: Sure-thing principle violations in prisoner's dilemma and two-stage gambles
Method: Quantum probability model with Hilbert-space belief-action states and unitary (Hamiltonian) evolution
Setup and data: Applied to published prisoner's dilemma and two-stage gamble results
Key result: Interference reproduces violations of the law of total probability that classical models cannot
Limitation: Parameters fitted to few aggregate data points; no new experiment

Phenomenon: Choosing between Markov and quantum dynamic models of decision
Method: Parameter-free tests of the law of total probability and the doubly stochastic law
Setup and data: New decision experiment plus review of published cognitive-psychology findings
Key result: Provides parameter-free tests discriminating Markov vs quantum models; evidence reviewed on both properties
Limitation: Conclusions tied to the specific paradigms; detailed results not read here

Phenomenon: Concept combination; membership weights for conjunctions and disjunctions
Method: Hilbert/Fock-space quantum model with superposition and interference; two-layer (logical/conceptual) thought
Setup and data: Reanalysis of Hampton (1988a,b) membership-weight data
Key result: Data shown incompatible with classical models; quantum model reproduces over- and underextension
Limitation: Post hoc reconstruction of existing data; model freedom high

Phenomenon: Foundations of quantum-like modelling in psychology, economics and finance
Method: Contextual probability; representation of interference data by complex/hyperbolic amplitudes
Setup and data: Monograph; theoretical development with illustrations from published data
Key result: Systematic quantum-like framework linking contextuality and interference to QP representations
Limitation: Applications largely illustrative; limited systematic model comparison

Phenomenon: Order effects in sequential evidence evaluation (inference)
Method: Quantum probability model with incompatible evidence perspectives; compared with belief-adjustment model
Setup and data: Mock-jury style judgement task with evidence presented in different orders
Key result: Quantum model reproduced the pattern of order effects better than the anchoring-and-adjustment model (per Bruza 2015)
Limitation: Vignette judgements; details of sample and fits not read here

Phenomenon: Probability judgement fallacies (conjunction, disjunction, inverse, conditional)
Method: Quantum probability with sequential projections onto incompatible subspaces
Setup and data: Theoretical comparison against published findings, including order effects in conjunction judgements
Key result: Quantum model explains more of 15 major findings than three rival theories
Limitation: Mostly qualitative evaluation; no new experiment

Phenomenon: Concept combination; entanglement between concepts
Method: SCoP/quantum modelling; CHSH Bell inequality test on exemplar choices
Setup and data: Choice experiment with 81 participants on the combination 'The Animal Acts'
Key result: CHSH value 2.4197 > 2, interpreted as violation of Bell's inequality
Limitation: Possible signalling/marginal-selectivity violations not addressed; single concept pair

Phenomenon: Concept combination, decision paradoxes and information retrieval
Method: SCoP formalism; Hilbert-space interference model; two-layer thought hypothesis
Setup and data: Conference overview of prior experiments and models; no new data
Key result: Argues quantum structure is a structural model for human and artificial thought; proposes SCoP-based knowledge organisation
Limitation: No new empirical or computational tests

Phenomenon: Sure-thing principle violations; disjunction effect (Hawaii problem)
Method: Quantum mechanical model of the decision situation within a two-layer (conceptual/logical) thought structure
Setup and data: Modelling of published Hawaii-problem data (Tversky & Shafir)
Key result: Quantum model reproduces 54%/57% vs 32% choice pattern as interference of conceptual landscape
Limitation: Single published data set; no predictive test

Phenomenon: Decision under risk and uncertainty; classical paradoxes
Method: Quantum Decision Theory: prospect states, utility factor plus interference (attraction) factor, entanglement
Setup and data: Theoretical framework applied to published paradox data
Key result: Explains disjunction effect, conjunction fallacy, Allais and Ellsberg-type paradoxes
Limitation: Interference factor only partly constrained; post hoc application

Phenomenon: Order effects, judgement errors, concepts, memory, decision dynamics
Method: Quantum probability and quantum dynamics (vs classical and Markov models)
Setup and data: Textbook synthesising models and published laboratory data
Key result: Unified QP account of multiple anomalies; comparisons with classical/Markov models
Limitation: Laboratory paradigms; the file covers only front matter and Chapter 1

Phenomenon: General case for QP cognitive modelling
Method: Quantum probability theory (superposition, incompatibility, entanglement) vs classical probability
Setup and data: Target article reviewing published empirical findings
Key result: Argues many judgement and decision anomalies have natural QP accounts
Limitation: Review/position; criticisms about flexibility raised in commentaries

Phenomenon: Programmatic case for quantum models of cognition
Method: Conceptual overview of QP principles (incompatibility, superposition, entanglement)
Setup and data: Special-issue introduction; no data
Key result: Frames QP as a general cognitive modelling framework and lists open questions
Limitation: Programmatic; no new evidence

Phenomenon: Question order effects in attitude surveys
Method: Quantum question-order model; parameter-free QQ equality
Setup and data: Tests on published survey order-effect data
Key result: QQ equality supported in the data examined
Limitation: Uses existing data; details of datasets not read here

Phenomenon: Concept combination and conceptual dynamics
Method: Hilbert/Fock-space modelling of concepts as context-dependent states; entanglement
Setup and data: Overview applying models to published membership-weight and combination data
Key result: Quantum models reproduce guppy-type effects, over/underextension and entanglement
Limitation: Mostly post hoc reconstruction of existing data

Phenomenon: Question order effects in national surveys
Method: Quantum question-order model; parameter-free QQ equality test
Setup and data: 70 national field surveys plus two laboratory experiments (as reported in Bruza 2015)
Key result: QQ equality statistically supported; anchoring-adjustment models fail to reproduce patterns
Limitation: Necessary but not sufficient evidence; replicability issue for projective models

Phenomenon: Consistency of quantum measurement models with order effects and response replicability
Method: Formal analysis of projective (Lüders) and generalised quantum measurement models
Setup and data: Theoretical no-go analysis referencing known empirical regularities
Key result: Projective quantum models cannot jointly reproduce order effects and response replicability
Limitation: Restricted measurement classes; resolved later via quantum instruments

Phenomenon: Review of quantum vs Bayesian models of judgement and decision
Method: Comparison of classical and quantum probability axioms; review of QP models
Setup and data: Review of published empirical findings
Key result: QP accounts for order effects, QQ equality (70 surveys), total-probability violations; classical and QP coincide for compatible events
Limitation: Review; no new data; dynamics and contextuality left as open questions

Phenomenon: Introduction to quantum cognition for psychologists
Method: Overview of QP principles (incompatibility, superposition) and applications
Setup and data: Short review; no new data
Key result: Summarises QP explanations of order effects, fallacies and sure-thing violations
Limitation: Brief; limited treatment of classical alternatives

Phenomenon: Choice-confidence interference in perceptual evidence accumulation
Method: Quantum random walk vs Markov random walk models
Setup and data: Random-dot motion task with confidence ratings, with and without an intermediate choice
Key result: Intermediate choice changed later confidence (interference); quantum walk fitted better than Markov
Limitation: Simple perceptual paradigm; sample and fit statistics not read here

Phenomenon: Tutorial on constructing quantum cognitive models
Method: Hilbert-space projections, non-commuting measurements, derivation of the QQ equality
Setup and data: Tutorial with worked example (order effects); no new data
Key result: Step-by-step construction of order-effect models and derivation of the QQ equality
Limitation: Ideal (pure-state, projective) models only

Phenomenon: Interference of categorisation on decision-making
Method: Belief-action entanglement (BAE) quantum model vs Markov and signal-detection models
Setup and data: Three face categorisation-decision experiments, 721 participants (C-D, X-D, D-alone trials)
Key result: Interference (violation of total probability) in some conditions; BAE model predicted the pattern
Limitation: Effect not present in all conditions; laboratory stimuli

Phenomenon: Effect of repeated judgements on belief change (quantum Zeno effect)
Method: Quantum model of belief evolution with repeated measurements
Setup and data: Behavioural experiments manipulating the number of intermediate judgements
Key result: Frequent judgements associated with slower belief change, consistent with a Zeno effect
Limitation: Classical commitment/consistency explanations must be ruled out; specific paradigm

Phenomenon: Foundations of quantum probability for measurement and decision-making
Method: Quantum Decision Theory: utility factor plus attraction factor; quarter law; information-dependent decay
Setup and data: Formal development with prisoner's dilemma illustration (Tversky & Shafir data)
Key result: Predicted 0.35/0.65 vs observed 0.37/0.63 cooperation/defection; conditions for classical reduction
Limitation: Single illustrative empirical comparison; largely formal

Phenomenon: Defining and testing contextuality in systems of random variables
Method: Contextuality-by-Default: bunches, connections, probabilistic couplings
Setup and data: Formal theory for finite categorical systems; no data
Key result: Criterion distinguishing true contextuality from direct context influences on marginals
Limitation: Diagnostic framework rather than a cognitive model

Phenomenon: Tutorial on advanced quantum-cognition tools
Method: Density matrices, POVMs, open-system dynamics
Setup and data: Methodological tutorial; no data
Key result: Framework for incorporating noise and imperfect measurement in QP models
Limitation: Added parameters increase flexibility

Phenomenon: Normative (rational) status of quantum probabilistic judgement
Method: Formal analysis of QP reasoning with respect to Dutch book-style rationality criteria
Setup and data: Theoretical analysis; details of any empirical component not verified
Key result: Argues QP reasoning can be principled rather than simply erroneous under incompatible perspectives
Limitation: Restricted notion of rationality; assumptions about elicitation

Phenomenon: Probabilistic inference judgements (order effects, inverse fallacy, Markov violations, anti-discounting)
Method: Hierarchy of QP models varying compatibility from fully quantum to classical
Setup and data: Three behavioural experiments; individual differences linked to Cognitive Reflection Test
Key result: Accounts for five inference phenomena; representations become more classical with task familiarity
Limitation: Extra flexibility in selecting hierarchy level; laboratory vignettes only

Phenomenon: Time evolution of mental states in decision-making
Method: Nested QPT models with Hamiltonian and Lindbladian (open-system) dynamics, pure and mixed initial states
Setup and data: Hypothetical decision paradigm; mathematical and numerical illustration
Key result: Clarifies relations and explanatory value of increasingly complex dynamics
Limitation: No empirical data; flexibility not tested against behaviour

Phenomenon: Conjunction fallacy
Method: Comparison of sequential (order-effect) and emergence (overextension) quantum models
Setup and data: World Wide Web queried sequentially and non-sequentially as an information space
Key result: Emergence effects, not order effects, identified as the main mechanism
Limitation: Web data as proxy for cognition; no individual-level participant data

Phenomenon: Question order effects and response replicability in sequential survey judgements
Method: General tension-reduction (GTR) hidden-measurement model on the extended Bloch sphere; exact non-Hilbertian solution
Setup and data: Re-analysis of Gallup poll data (Moore, 2002): Clinton/Gore and Rose/Jackson question pairs; theoretical treatment of response replicability
Key result: Exact fits to both data sets; argues the data are irreducibly non-Hilbertian, that the QQ-equality can hold for non-Hilbertian models, and that order effects plus replicability are jointly modelled
Limitation: Descriptive fit to aggregate published data; no new experiment or predictive test; flexible model with added fluctuation parameters

Phenomenon: Context effects across subsets of judged variables
Method: Hilbert space multidimensional (HSM) quantum probability models
Setup and data: New large behavioural experiment; comparison with Bayesian network models
Key result: HSM fits compare favourably with Bayesian networks, demonstrating viability
Limitation: Classical comparison limited to Bayesian networks; dimension choice by modeller

Phenomenon: Contextuality in paired human choices
Method: Contextuality-by-Default analysis of a Bell-type (EPR/Bohm) choice design
Setup and data: Crowdsourced experiment with characters and traits from The Snow Queen
Key result: Marginal selectivity violated, yet true contextuality detected beyond direct influences
Limitation: Artificial task engineered for contextuality; generality unclear

Phenomenon: Belief change during evidence monitoring; sequential probability ratings
Method: Quantum random-walk (Schrödinger) model vs Markov random-walk model and Markov with drift variability; generalisation criterion
Setup and data: 11 participants, ~1000 dot-motion trials each, 4 coherence levels (2–16%), three rating-time conditions
Key result: Small interference effects (low coherence; 3/11 participants); summed G² diff favoured quantum (350, 306, 260, 40), but versus Markov with drift variability quantum wins only at low coherence
Limitation: Small sample; single perceptual task; advantage shrinks against a stronger Markov baseline

Phenomenon: True contextuality versus direct influences in human decisions
Method: Contextuality-by-Default analysis; reanalysis of prior data plus new experiments
Setup and data: Crowdsourcing experiments extending the Snow Queen design
Key result: Prior claimed demonstrations explained by direct influences; new experiments show true contextuality
Limitation: Specially designed tasks; ecological prevalence unknown

Phenomenon: Dynamics of choice, confidence and decision time
Method: Open-system (Lindblad) quantum–Markov master equation with quantum/Markov weight
Setup and data: Theoretical formulation with numerical illustration (101-dimensional state space)
Key result: Unifies random-walk and quantum-walk dynamics in one process
Limitation: Methodological; empirical fits reported elsewhere

Phenomenon: Question order effect combined with response replicability
Method: Theory of non-atomic quantum instruments
Setup and data: Mathematical construction; no new data
Key result: Shows both effects can be jointly modelled, overturning the no-go for this class
Limitation: No empirical fit; interpretation of added freedom unconstrained

Phenomenon: Decision making over time; dynamic inconsistency
Method: Quantum decision theory with utility and attraction factors; quantum intelligence network
Setup and data: Review with theoretical illustrations
Key result: Argues dynamic inconsistencies are resolved in QDT; quantum-classical correspondence
Limitation: Largely theoretical; parameters set by general arguments

Phenomenon: Constructed preference and effect of prior choice on preference strength
Method: Open-system model combining Markov random walk and quantum dynamics
Setup and data: Two behavioural experiments tracking preference strength over time
Key result: Oscillating preference strength and choice-induced shifts captured by the open-system model
Limitation: Laboratory tasks; effects shown at the level of mean preference

Phenomenon: Joint modelling of question order effect, response replicability and QQ-equality
Method: Quantum instruments (general quantum measurement theory) with generalised Wang–Busemeyer postulates
Setup and data: Formal construction; application to Clinton–Gore Gallup poll data (Moore, 2002)
Key result: Instruments satisfying QOE, RRE and QQE exist; model closely reproduces Clinton–Gore statistics with an order-independent prior state
Limitation: Single published data set; existence proof rather than competitive model comparison; no new experiment

Phenomenon: Preferential choice and response time
Method: Open-system (Markov + quantum random walk) model versus pure Markov and pure quantum models
Setup and data: New gift-card preferential choice experiment; model comparison by AIC, BIC and chi-squared
Key result: Pure Markov model favoured for most participants; a substantial number required the open system model
Limitation: Benefit limited to a subset of participants; single task domain

Phenomenon: Quantum-like modelling of biological and cognitive information processing
Method: Open quantum systems theory: quantum instruments and quantum master equation; QBism interpretation
Setup and data: Review; no new data
Key result: Argues open-system formalism is the natural basis for quantum-like biology and cognition
Limitation: Conceptual breadth; little direct empirical validation

Phenomenon: Foundational framework for contextual probability update covering classical and quantum measurements
Method: Contextual measurement model (CMM) on contextual probability spaces; links to quantum instruments and generalised probability theory
Setup and data: Formal development with illustrative examples; no empirical data
Key result: Kolmogorov, von Neumann and quantum-instrument measurements framed within CMM; contextual definitions of order effect, response replicability, interference and Bell-type violations
Limitation: Purely theoretical; arXiv preprint; no empirical test or cognitive application worked out in detail

Phenomenon: Constructive memory; sequential measurement effects
Method: Temporal Bell inequality test
Setup and data: Two memory experiments with a novel change-judgement task
Key result: Violation of a temporal Bell inequality observed in one case
Limitation: Violation in only one case; suggestive evidence

Phenomenon: Conjunction fallacy: coverage of possible probability-judgement patterns in the literature
Method: Extensional (factual) analysis of the [0,1]^3 space of P(A), P(B), P(A∧B); literature compilation
Setup and data: 4080 articles citing Tversky & Kahneman (1983) to 2016; 272 with probability-estimate experiments; 37 with full reporting; 416 data points
Key result: Data cluster in a few sub-volumes; single fallacy well explored, no-fallacy and double-fallacy regions under-explored
Limitation: Descriptive only; coarse binning; depends on reporting practices; no new experiment or model

Phenomenon: Probability judgement fallacies
Method: Quantum Sequential Sampler combining Bayesian/quantum reasoning with sequential sampling
Setup and data: New large probability-judgement experiment; comparison with the Bayesian Sampler
Key result: Model compared favourably with the Bayesian Sampler; systematic overestimation of probabilities discovered
Limitation: Complex model; single main classical competitor

Phenomenon: Recognition heuristic and hindsight bias in paired-comparison judgements
Method: Quantum-controlled unitary operator (circuit formalism) combined with quantum sequential sampling
Setup and data: Tutorial/poster; illustrative calculation for a city-size comparison (Frankfurt vs Mainz) in an ABA paradigm
Key result: Deterministic heuristic recovered under measurement; probabilistic choice and hindsight bias emerge from superposition and projective update
Limitation: Short poster paper; no quantitative model fitting reported; classical probabilistic heuristics capture some of the same features

Phenomenon: Characterising measurement classes for question order, response replicability and QQ-equality
Method: Quantum measurement theory; sharp repeatable non-projective (SRP̄) instruments; observable vs state-update non-commutativity
Setup and data: Formal analysis; no new empirical data
Key result: SRP̄ measurements reproduce QOE with RRE and can satisfy or violate the QQ-equality; non-classicality can arise from non-commuting state-update maps with commuting observables
Limitation: Theoretical; speculative link between SRP̄ and conscious processing; no empirical model comparison

Phenomenon: Temporal dynamics of deliberation and decision, including strategic games
Method: GKSL (Lindblad) open-system master equation; passive vs active Hamiltonians; spectral analysis of 'cognitive beats'
Setup and data: Theoretical analysis and illustrative dynamics; Prisoner's Dilemma example; proposed experimental designs
Key result: Framework linking GKSL steady states to decisions, stabilisation of non-Nash outcomes, and predicted beat envelopes in conviction
Limitation: No new data; predictions (beats) untested; arXiv preprint

Phenomenon: Word association and cued recall in the mental lexicon
Method: Quantum-theoretic models of word association
Setup and data: Theoretical modelling of intralist/extralist association results; proposed experiments
Key result: Initial quantum models outlined and experimental tests proposed
Limitation: Exploratory; no new discriminating experiment

Phenomenon: Borderline vagueness and borderline contradictions
Method: Classical Hopfield-network probabilistic model versus quantum probability with interference
Setup and data: Theoretical analysis of existing experimental findings
Key result: Classical model falls short; quantum interference explains borderline contradictions
Limitation: No new data; relies on existing experiments

Phenomenon: Similarity judgement (asymmetry, triangle inequality, diagnosticity)
Method: Quantum geometric model with concept subspaces and sequential projection
Setup and data: Theoretical demonstrations against Tversky's (1977) findings
Key result: Asymmetry as order effect; triangle-inequality and diagnosticity effects accommodated
Limitation: Little new empirical fitting

Phenomenon: Episodic recognition memory: over-distribution and subadditivity
Method: Generalized Quantum Episodic Memory (GQEM) model versus dual-trace OD model
Setup and data: Novel item-memory experiment plus published source-memory data
Key result: GQEM accounts for over-distribution and subadditivity
Limitation: Limited paradigms; single classical competitor

Phenomenon: Effect of episodic memory of prior judgements on later judgements (AA, AB/BA, ABA paradigms)
Method: System-plus-environment measurement models and quantum instruments; comparison of OK, BB and new OB accounts
Setup and data: Theoretical comparison against published question-order and response-replicability findings
Key result: All three accounts cover the combined findings but differ in mechanism (belief-type updates vs non-commuting projections) and in allowing changed answers on repeated questions
Limitation: No new data or quantitative fit; ABA empirical evidence contested

Phenomenon: Biases in probability judgement
Method: Probability theory plus noise (PT+N) model
Setup and data: Two behavioural experiments
Key result: Near-normative judgements for noise-cancelling expressions; four biases explained by noise
Limitation: Does not address all phenomena targeted by quantum models (e.g. sequential order effects)

Phenomenon: Conjunction fallacy
Method: Derivation of testable predictions of quantum-like models; experimental-economics test
Setup and data: Incentivised experiment in a question-order configuration
Key result: Results at odds with quantum-like model predictions
Limitation: Targets a specific class of quantum-like models

Phenomenon: Contextuality in behavioural and social data
Method: Contextuality-by-Default analysis of cyclic binary systems
Setup and data: Reanalysis of opinion polls, visual illusions, conjoint choices, word combinations, psychophysical matching
Key result: No evidence of true contextuality in the reviewed datasets
Limitation: Based on existing datasets; later designed experiments found contextuality

Phenomenon: Question order effects in opinion polls
Method: Comparison of quantum projection model vs classical (real-valued) projection model; interpretation of rotation parameters
Setup and data: Clinton–Gore Gallup poll data (Moore, 2002); 2-dimensional decision space
Key result: Both models reproduce the order effects; interference terms play no role, so the classical projection model suffices
Limitation: Single data set; low-dimensional toy setting; does not address interference-based paradigms

Phenomenon: Sequential opinion measurement (ABA design)
Method: Test of quantum measurement-disturbance predictions
Setup and data: 325 MTurk participants; 12 pairs of opinion questions on 0–100 scale
Key result: Moderate changes in repeated A judgements; correlation pattern consistent with quantum predictions
Limitation: Online opinion ratings; low-stakes judgements

Phenomenon: Mirrored question order effects (QQ equality)
Method: Classical-probability process models of order effects
Setup and data: Theoretical analysis of existing order-effect findings
Key result: Classical models can reproduce mirrored order effects
Limitation: Shows possibility rather than superiority of classical accounts

Phenomenon: Invariants in probabilistic reasoning (QQ, addition law, Bayes rule identities)
Method: Probability theory plus noise analysis
Setup and data: Analysis of identities in probability judgement data
Key result: Identities hold despite biases; consistent with noisy classical reasoning
Limitation: Aggregate identities only; not all quantum-targeted phenomena addressed

Phenomenon: Choice under uncertainty; Prisoner's Dilemma (sure-thing principle violation)
Method: Quantum stochastic walk on a cognitive network; Lindblad–Kossakowski master equation interpolating unitary and dissipative dynamics; Luce choice axiom for profitability
Setup and data: Analytical model with Prisoner's Dilemma case study; no new participant data
Key result: Stationary distribution of the QSW yields choice probabilities that can violate the law of total probability / sure-thing principle; unique stationary state proved (Spohn's theorem)
Limitation: Toy illustration only; several free parameters; not tested against new human data

Phenomenon: Contextuality in two-person strategic interaction
Method: Classical vs quantum (entangled-state) probability models fitted to joint choice data
Setup and data: Two online experiments with a PD-variant without Nash equilibrium; Exp. 1 N = 100
Key result: Evidence of sensitivity to context; quantum model fitted better than a matched classical model
Limitation: Single task family; classical baseline limited; entanglement interpreted as epiphenomenal

Phenomenon: Neural implementation of quantum cognition operations
Method: Mapping of QP operations (states, projections, unitary evolution) onto classical neural mechanisms such as oscillations
Setup and data: Theoretical paper; no new data
Key result: Proposes classical neural realisations of quantum-cognition operations (no quantitative results)
Limitation: Not tested against neural data

Phenomenon: Neural basis of quantum-like decision statistics
Method: Quantum information representation of neuronal states; GKSL (Lindblad) open-system dynamics; decision as decoherence to a steady state
Setup and data: Theoretical model; no data
Key result: Decision state is a steady state reached with exponentially fast convergence (analytical)
Limitation: No empirical neural test; mapping of neurons to qubit-like states is hypothetical

Phenomenon: Neural grounding of quantum-like cognition
Method: Generalised probability theory linking neuronal network descriptions with quantum-like cognitive models
Setup and data: Theoretical paper
Key result: Formal coupling proposed; no quantitative results known
Limitation: No empirical test; details not re-checked

Phenomenon: Neural oscillations as a substrate for quantum-like cognition and AI
Method: Mapping oscillatory neuronal network dynamics onto quantum-like state representations; implications for quantum-inspired computing
Setup and data: Theoretical paper
Key result: Conceptual/formal bridge proposed; no quantitative results known
Limitation: No empirical test; details not re-checked

Phenomenon: Neural grounding of quantum-like entanglement in cognition ('mental entanglement')
Method: Prequantum classical statistical field theory / generalised probability; observation entanglement via local operator algebras; state entanglement from coupled oscillatory networks
Setup and data: Theoretical; proposed EEG/MEG, in vitro network and Bell-inequality experimental designs; no data collected
Key result: Formal construction showing how classical neuronal networks can yield QL entangled states and observables; mapping to EEG/MEG functional connectivity measures
Limitation: Conceptual only; no empirical test; biophysical mechanism admitted to be unclear; speculative links to binding and consciousness
